acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Djinn family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Djinn, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Ring-Vector Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Sharply defined figure with ornate sashes and jewelry, arms of visibly swirling wind, and gold rings orbiting the forearms.
Signature mechanic: Three-Wish Vector: three gold rings align around one visible wind forearm, then release pressure lanes in outer-to-inner order while the other arm stays still.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a directional controller that separates visible wind-arm direction from orbiting-ring release order.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 vapor, half-face, and trailing plume gain an invisible pressure cinch; T2 the defined torso and plain cuffs gain directional channels; T3 visible wind arms and orbiting rings gain calibrated vanes; T4 crown and sacred script gain pressure glyphs; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps gain bounded throne gauges.

Motion/process branches use an additional pressure process with tiered apparatus: T1 the vapor half-face routes its plume around a still cinch; T2 the torso vents through one cuff channel; T3 the wind arms drive orbiting-ring vanes; T4 crown script redirects one pressure glyph; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps drive and still one throne gauge.
counterplay: Move through the still arm's lane and strike the widest ring gap before the inner release. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the vapor half-face exposes its still plume-cinch apparatus after the directional rush; T2 the torso cuff opens its still channel after venting; T3 wind arms and orbiting rings expose the vane anchor between releases; T4 crown script exposes the still pressure glyph between clauses; T5 vortex, throne, and lamps expose the throne gauge at its still interval.
forbiddenTreatments: Native hovering or vortex motion alone presented as Wind affinity
identityInvariants: A hovering humanoid upper body tapers into smoke instead of legs; solidity and scale change only at explicit tiers.
Sapphire or violet smoke, warm inner light, gold, brass, turquoise, silk, and gemstones remain distinct source materials.
Cuffs, rings, headpieces, lamps, and script mark proposed binding status without establishing universal culture or morality.
The body becomes less solid and more spatially dominant from half-face vapor to a palace-scale throne vortex.
telegraph: Ornate sash tails stream in one direction and the three forearm rings click into visibly unequal spacing.
